thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Detected spike of 5xx errors on /v1/generate in us-east-1. Creating incident INC-20270315-01 and opening war room. War room: https://warroom.redwood.app/INC-20270315-01 (auto-created). Paging on-call now.
Anya: acked the page. i'm joining war room. severity set to P1 until impact confirmed.
Marco: oncall here, seeing alerts too. paging still working. i'll take initial triage.
Eli: I'll take ownership of the incident. assigning to @Eli. Triage steps: confirm blast radius, check model fallback, check autoscaler logs.
Maya: CS heads-up: got a support ticket from Acme saying timeouts and partial responses. Potentially multiple customers — prioritizing enterprise customers.
Rachel: product note: if customers are affected, we'll prepare a status page component and a short customer email. I'll draft text and iterate here.
Anya: @Marco @Eli confirm pager delivery? Did PagerDuty escalate to phone for primary? ops-pager shows 1 ack from Marco and 1 ack from Anya.
Marco: PagerDuty shows escalation to phone eventually but both acked via mobile. Confirmed.
Kim: quick check: recent deploy in us-east-1 18m ago that touched runtime config for batching. I'm pulling deploy logs now.
Eli: initial hypothesis: batching config regression + GC pressure on a subset of GPU hosts. checking host metrics and agent logs.
Anya: creating checklist in war room:
- Owner: Eli (investigate & coordinate)
- On-call: Marco (pager), Anya (sre backup)
- CS contact: Maya
- Product comms: Rachel
- ENG mitigation: Kim
- War room link: https://warroom.redwood.app/INC-20270315-01
Marco: I'm running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep us-east-1` and tailing the runtime logs.
Kim: logs show repeated `KVCache OOM` followed by retries on host gpux-12. snippet:
```
2027-03-15T12:07:10Z runtime ERROR KVCache OOM key=ctx-... size=128MB
2027-03-15T12:07:11Z runtime WARN retrying request id=abc123
2027-03-15T12:07:12Z runtime ERROR request-handler 5xx status=502 url=/v1/generate
```
Eli: mitigation options:
1) Roll back recent batching config change (fast but may require deploy)
2) Route traffic away from affected GPU pool to fallback pool (instant, might increase cost)
3) Enable model-level small-seq fallback variant (trades quality for stability)
Which do we prefer for minimal customer impact?
Marco: route traffic to fallback pool first, keep Canary capacity warm. I'll open a routing change PR and request hotflip.
Anya: if we route, update the status page as 'degraded performance' and note that mitigation is in progress.
Rachel: draft status page update (ready to post):
```
Status: Degraded performance in US-East-1
Impact: Some requests to the text generation API (/v1/generate) may return errors or experience increased latency for certain workloads.
Started: 2027-03-15 12:07 UTC
Customer impact: Some customers may see failed requests or partial responses. We are actively mitigating.
Next update: in 10 minutes or sooner.
```
Maya: draft customer email for enterprise contacts (short):
```
Subject: Incident affecting text generation API in US-East-1
Hi — we’re investigating an issue impacting the /v1/generate endpoint in US-East-1 which may cause errors or increased latency. Our team has identified the root area and is actively mitigating. We’ll follow up within 30 minutes with more details. If this is causing a production outage for you, reply and we’ll prioritize.
— Redwood Inference Support
```
Eli: good. @Rachel please prepare to post the status page update and hold the customer email until we have confirmation of mitigation.
Marco: routing change in progress — applying a temporary traffic rule to route 30% of traffic to fallback pool and 70% to primary to avoid overload. Command used:
```
redwood route update --pool us-east-1-primary --fallback us-east-1-fallback --split 70:30 --dry-run=false
```
Kim: observed immediate drop in error rate on subset after applying 30/70. still monitoring.
Anya: Confirming communication steps:
- Post status page update (Rachel)
- Send targeted customer note to enterprise customers if mitigation not confirmed in 30m (Maya)
- Keep war room open, cadence every 10m for updates (Anya)
- Escalate to infra oncall if routing doesn't stabilize in 20m (Eli)
Rachel: posting status page now. Will paste final verbatim to the war room once posted.
incident-bot: Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270315-01
Eli: monitoring metrics and error budget dashboards. current error rate: 12% -> after routing change 4.2%. holding for 5m confirmation.
Maya: CS has initial outreach to top 5 enterprise customers, awaiting responses. no direct escalations to execs yet.
Marco: will stay on war room for the next 40m, then hand off to Eli for continued mitigation — Eli pls confirm you can take the handoff at +40m.
Eli: confirmed, I'll take over at +40m and coordinate escalation if needed. @Anya please record action items in the incident tracker.
Anya: recorded. next update in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Kim: creating follow-up ticket to revert batching config and run a canary once stable. ticket: RED-7891
Rachel: prepping customer-facing postmortem template to be ready after incident closes.
Maya: closing loop on CS: will provide customers the 30min follow-up and let them know we're monitoring.
Marco: thanks team. quick note: if anyone gets a phone from PagerDuty, please confirm ack here. otherwise i'll post a short handoff before I leave.
Eli: acknowledged. good work so far. continuing investigation and will update in 10.
